__prompts__.project_slug: Machine-readable package and repository name. Consumers apply their own additional slug constraints.
__prompts__.project_short_description: One-sentence description used in README and package metadata.
__prompts__.project_long_description: Longer public description of the project motivation and scope.
__prompts__.development_status: Current repostatus.org lifecycle status for the software.
__prompts__.keywords: Public keywords used in package metadata, citation metadata, registries, and archives.
__prompts__.contributors: Everyone credited for the software, each entry declaring one or more roles. Name and roles are required; entries may also include given_names, family_names, email, affiliations, orcid, and url. A non-empty list must credit at least one author, which is what citation metadata requires.
__prompts__.funding: Public funding records. Entries may include funder, award_number, award_title, grant_url, and project_code.
__prompts__.motivation: Public purpose, purpose categories, problem statement, and value proposition.
__prompts__.related_software: Related or upstream tools. Entries may include name, url_or_doi, and relationship.
__prompts__.urls: Canonical source repository, project homepage, and published documentation URLs.
__prompts__.registries: Registry entries such as PyPI, CRAN, bio.tools, WorkflowHub, or institutional catalogues. Entries may include name, url_or_id, and notes.
__prompts__.persistent_identifiers: Persistent identifiers. Each entry declares its CFF identifier type and value, with an optional associated version.
__prompts__.publications: Associated publications. Entries may include title, type, authors, doi, pmid, pmcid, url, citation, note, and preferred.
__prompts__.licensing: License text or SPDX identifier and the selected dependency-license compatibility method.
__prompts__.include_metadata: Whether the project publishes CodeMeta and Citation File Format metadata files alongside their validation workflow.
__prompts__.documentation_builder: Optional documentation site generator. An empty selection means documentation is plain Markdown.
__prompts__.documentation_types: SMP documentation categories the project provides. API and technical reference material are part of developer documentation.
__prompts__.community_files: Standard root community files the project provides. CONTRIBUTING.md and SUPPORT.md imply the corresponding GitHub collaboration files.
__prompts__.support_routes: Public support, bug-reporting, or feature-request systems and their public URLs.
__prompts__.contacts: Public contact routes for general community, code-of-conduct, and private security reports.
__prompts__.programming_languages: Programming languages used by the project. Entries include a name and may include version_constraint and role from the SMP.
__prompts__.software_functions: Functions or operations performed by the software. Entries may include summary, operation, input, output, cmd, and note.
__prompts__.interfaces: Interfaces exposed by the software. Type names the interface; specification and status describe it.
__prompts__.operating_systems: Supported operating systems or platforms. Entries may include name, specification, and status from the SMP.
__prompts__.external_dependencies: External software dependencies or standards. Entries may include name, version_constraint, url, license, and purpose.
__prompts__.external_services: External public services, partners, or roles needed by the project. Entries may include name, provider, service_types, quantity, and cost_coverage.
__prompts__.test_types: Types of tests used or desired. Supported values match the SMP testing checklist.
__prompts__.test_frameworks: Testing frameworks used by the project.
__prompts__.quality_tools: Optional primary formatter, linter, and static type checker.
__prompts__.project_manager: Primary project and dependency manager, which determines setup, command execution, lockfile handling, and CI.
__prompts__.versioning: Version value and public release policy. Empty properties leave the policy unspecified.
__prompts__.distribution_channels: Controlled public distribution routes, including package registries, releases, archives, installers, and hosted services.
__prompts__.containerization: Container recipes the project ships. Project managers and lockfiles are declared separately.
__prompts__.resource_requirements: Public typical and worst-case memory, storage, compute, GPU, wall-clock, or scaling requirements.
__prompts__.maintenance_level: Public maintenance commitment after active development winds down; leave empty when no commitment is declared.
__prompts__.retirement_criteria: Public conditions under which the software may be retired.
__prompts__.public_risk_notes: Public risk or mitigation notes. Sensitive security, privacy, or compliance details should not be included.
__prompts__.regulatory_requirements: Controlled and additional public regulatory, quality, policy, or availability requirements.
__prompts__.security_measures: Controlled and additional public security measures protecting the software and its data.
__prompts__.data_management: Public sensitive-data statement and DMP reference or contact route.

project_slug.description: Use an R package name of at least two ASCII letters, digits, or dots; start with a letter and do not end with a dot.
